chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from al-Hasan al-Bazzaz, that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, peace be upon them both, said:

"Shall I not inform you of the most important duty Allah has imposed upon His creation?" I said: "Yes, please do." He said: "To treat people justly as you would yourself, to share generously with your brother, and to remember Allah in every situation.

And by remembrance, I do not mean saying 'Glory be to Allah,' 'Praise be to Allah,' 'There is no god but Allah,' and 'Allah is the Greatest' — though this is indeed part of it — but rather remembering Allah in every circumstance where you are confronted with obedience to Allah or disobedience to Him."

key_terms.إنصاف: Insaf — treating people justly and equitably, measuring their rights as equal to your own
key_terms.ذكر الله: Dhikr Allah — remembrance of Allah; here redefined from verbal formulae to active God-consciousness in moral decisions
key_terms.طاعة: Ta'a — obedience to Allah; following His commands
key_terms.معصية: Ma'siya — disobedience to Allah; sinning against His commands
key_terms.مواساة: Muwasaat — sharing generously with others, especially in times of need; fraternal solidarity

ai.seo_question: What are the three most important duties according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS), through a reliable chain from Zurara ibn A'yan, identifies the three most important duties Allah has imposed: treating people with the same fairness you expect for yourself (insaf), sharing generously with your fellow believer (muwasaat), and being conscious of Allah in every situation. The Imam clarifies that 'remembrance of Allah' is not merely verbal dhikr formulas like tasbeeh and tahleel, but a constant God-consciousness that governs one's choices when facing decisions of obedience or sin.
